# Usage oracle goldens (`B0-4` + aggregation oracle)

Two layers of TokenTracker-derived baselines, both generated from the same
sanitized fixture home (`test/fixtures/usage/home`, 34 KiB synthetic):

| File | Layer | Compared by |
|---|---|---|
| `queue-rows.json` | bucket-level: TT `queue.jsonl` replayed as LWW by `source\|model\|hour_start` (11 buckets) | `--hl-db <usage.db>` against `usage_bucket` |
| `summary.json` | bucket-level rollup: per source/day and per model/day token sums | same (inside `--hl-db`) |
| `aggregates-asia-shanghai.json` | aggregation-level: TT local API payloads, `tz=Asia/Shanghai` | `--aggregates <hl-payloads.json>` |
| `aggregates-utc.json` | aggregation-level: TT local API payloads, `tz=UTC` | `--aggregates <hl-payloads.json>` |

## Aggregation goldens

Generated by:

```bash
node scripts/usage-oracle-check.js --tt-aggregates-only
```

That command (1) runs the fully local TT sync against the fixture home
(fresh `.tokentracker/` scratch, no device token, `Uploaded: skipped`), (2)
starts TokenTracker's real local API — `tracker.js serve --no-open --no-sync
--port <free loopback port>` with `USERPROFILE/HOME/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA`
redirected to the fixture home, `TOKENTRACKER_WSL_MODE=native-only`,
`TOKENTRACKER_NO_TELEMETRY=1`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` — (3) fetches (4) stops the
server. Goldens are byte-deterministic across runs (`md5sum` stable).

### Schema (`usage-oracle-aggregates-v1`)

```jsonc
{
  "schema": "usage-oracle-aggregates-v1",
  "generator": "scripts/usage-oracle-check.js --tt-aggregates-only",
  "tt_version": "1.4.7",
  "home": "test/fixtures/usage/home",
  "tz": "Asia/Shanghai",                    // or "UTC"
  "row_count": 11,                          // queue buckets fed to TT
  "local_days": ["2026-03-14", "..."],      // days with usage in this tz
  "period_definitions": { "day": "...", "week": "...", "month": "...", "total": "..." },
  "ranges": {                               // the concrete from/to queried
    "day":   { "from": "2026-03-16", "to": "2026-03-16" },
    "week":  { "from": "2026-03-16", "to": "2026-03-22" },   // Monday-start
    "month": { "from": "2026-03-01", "to": "2026-03-31" },
    "total": { "from": "2026-03-14", "to": "2026-03-16" }    // fixture span
  },
  "summary": { "day|week|month|total": { "from", "to", "days", "totals": {"input_tokens", ...}, "rolling": {...} } },
  "daily":   { "day|week|month|total": { "from", "to", "rows": [{ "day", "<8 ints>" }] } },
  "breakdown": { "day|week|month|total": { "from", "to", "sources": [{ "source", "source_scope", "totals", "models": [{ "model", "totals" }] }] } },
  "heatmap": { "weeks": 52, "week_starts_on": "sun", "active_days", "streak_days", "cells": [{ "day", "total_tokens", "billable_total_tokens", "level" }] },
  "notes": { "heatmap": "...", "cost": "...", "rolling": "...", "total_period": "..." }
}
```

Period semantics (TT's HTTP API takes only `from`/`to`; the dashboard computes
periods, so the fixture-era periods are pinned here):

- `day` = the latest fixture local day that has usage.
- `week` = Monday-start 7-day week containing that day (TT dashboard weeks start
  Monday). For this fixture the latest day is 2026-03-16, a Monday, so the week
  window has one active day — faithful to TT period semantics.
- `month` = calendar month containing that day.
- `total` = fixture span (`local_days[0]..local_days[-1]`) — a bounded stand-in
  for TT's rolling 24-month total, which is not reproducible against fixed
  fixture dates.

Timezone parity is real, not cosmetic: the UTC and Asia/Shanghai goldens differ
because the Codex `2026-03-15T23:30Z` bucket falls on 2026-03-16 in Shanghai
(2026-03-15 day totals differ: UTC 15,650 vs Shanghai 9,450 tokens). That is the
local-day grouping invariant the Highlighter aggregation must reproduce.

### Why TT's local API is the fast aggregation oracle

- `serve` needs **no account and no dashboard build** on this machine: the
  `tokentracker-cli@1.4.7` npm package ships `dashboard/dist/`, so
  `resolveDashboardDir()` succeeds; `--no-open` avoids a browser.
- The `/functions/tokentracker-usage-*` GET endpoints require no auth token
  (`/api/local-auth` exists for dashboard mutations only). Loopback only.
- Exact command (port chosen free; any free port works):

```bash
USERPROFILE=<repo>/test/fixtures/usage/home \
APPDATA=<repo>/test/fixtures/usage/home/AppData/Roaming \
LOCALAPPDATA=<repo>/test/fixtures/usage/home/AppData/Local \
TOKENTRACKER_WSL_MODE=native-only \
TOKENTRACKER_NO_TELEMETRY=1 DO_NOT_TRACK=1 \
node D:/workspace/_tt-oracle/node_modules/tokentracker-cli/bin/tracker.js \
  serve --no-open --no-sync --port <free-port>
```

Endpoints used (all `GET`, add `tz=` and `from=`/`to=` day keys):

| Endpoint | Params |
|---|---|
| `/functions/tokentracker-usage-summary` | `from`, `to`, `tz` |
| `/functions/tokentracker-usage-daily` | `from`, `to`, `tz` |
| `/functions/tokentracker-usage-model-breakdown` | `from`, `to`, `tz` |
| `/functions/tokentracker-usage-heatmap` | `weeks` (52), `tz` |

Caveats: `serve` kicks off an optional background pricing refresh that may do
one outbound fetch when no pricing cache exists (graceful seed fallback; cost is
out of scope for this page). The queue must exist before `serve --no-sync`;
`--tt-aggregates-only` runs the sync itself.

## Capturing the Highlighter side (`--aggregates`)

Once the usage feature/IPC is wired, capture the real IPC responses against the
same fixture home and write one JSON file:

```jsonc
{
  "schema": "hl-usage-aggregates-v1",
  "captures": [
    { "tz": "Asia/Shanghai", "view": "summary",   "period": "day",   "payload": <usage:summary response> },
    { "tz": "Asia/Shanghai", "view": "daily",     "period": "day",   "payload": <usage:daily response> },
    { "tz": "Asia/Shanghai", "view": "breakdown", "period": "day",   "payload": <usage:breakdown response> },
    { "tz": "Asia/Shanghai", "view": "heatmap",   "period": "total", "payload": <usage:heatmap response> }
    // ... day/week/month/total for summary/daily/breakdown, then heatmap; repeat for "UTC"
  ]
}
```

26 entries total are expected (2 tz × (4 periods × 3 views + 1 heatmap)).
Aliases accepted: `response`/`data`/`body` instead of `payload`; view
`model-breakdown`; `timezone` instead of `tz`; or a nested
`{ "<tz>": { "<view>": { "<period>": payload } } }` map. Payload shapes are read
tolerantly (`totals` / `data.rows` / `sources` / `weeks` etc. — see
`extract*` helpers in `scripts/usage-oracle-check.js`).

```bash
node scripts/usage-oracle-check.js --aggregates <captured-hl-payloads.json> [--json]
# exit 0 PASS / 1 mismatch / 2 unusable input or missing goldens
```

Comparison rules:

- **Zero tolerance** on integer token columns and `conversation_count` for
  `summary` (all 8 counters) and `daily` (per-day 7 token columns +
  conversation_count). Extra zero-filled days in a Highlighter daily payload are
  ignored (payloads may zero-fill the requested range); extra non-zero days are
  diffs.
- `breakdown`: per-source and per-model `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`,
  `cached_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens` with zero tolerance;
  `total_tokens`/`billable_total_tokens`/`reasoning_output_tokens`/
  `conversation_count` compared when the Highlighter payload provides them;
  `sharePct` (optional) within **0.01 percentage point** of the TT token share
  (`total_tokens` share of the range).
- `heatmap`: **day/value/level cell sets only** — TT computes its 52-week grid
  from the server run date and `week_starts_on:"sun"`, so column/week alignment
  drifts daily and is deliberately ignored. Active cells must match
  `billable_total_tokens` value and max-relative level with zero tolerance.
  `active_days` compared when present.
- **Cost is out of scope** (Q2: no money on the page): `total_cost_usd`,
  `pricing`, `cost_source` are stripped from goldens and never compared.
- `rolling.last_7d/last_30d`: TT derives the windows from the machine's current
  date, so only `active_days`, `billable_total_tokens`, `conversation_count`
  (and `avg_per_active_day` for 30d) are stored/compared when the Highlighter
  payload includes `rolling`.

`node scripts/usage-oracle-check.js --self-test` exercises the comparator with
synthetic payloads: exact match PASS, +1 token FAIL, missing source FAIL,
shifted heatmap grid PASS, cost-only drift PASS, zero-filled extra day PASS,
missing heatmap day FAIL.

## Refresh commands

```bash
node scripts/usage-oracle-check.js --build-fixtures        # synthetic inputs
node scripts/usage-oracle-check.js --tt-only --sync         # bucket goldens
node scripts/usage-oracle-check.js --tt-aggregates-only     # aggregation goldens
node scripts/usage-oracle-check.js --self-test              # comparator self-test
```
